issues.description: Constructor arity mismatch for the animal classes: the template's Main.java (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, lines 9-11) contains commented example usages that call two-argument constructors for Seal, Pig, and Goat (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")). The problem statement UML (problem_statement.md, lines 26-29) declares Animal with a single attribute name: String, and the solution implementation provides single-parameter constructors that accept only the name (Seal.java constructor at solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 7; Pig.java constructor at solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Pig.java line 5; Goat.java constructor at solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java line 5). This inconsistency can mislead students about the expected constructor signatures and which attributes they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor usage consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the commented example usages in the template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java (lines 9-11) to call single-argument constructors that match the UML and solution (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")). Alternatively, if additional attributes were intended, update the problem statement UML and the solution classes to declare and initialize the extra attribute(s) and implement corresponding two-argument constructors; document the intended constructor parameters clearly.
